meta.title: AI Infrastructure Deal Database
meta.subtitle: Financing structures, credit support, and transactions behind the compute buildout
meta.coverage: Project and structured financings, credit support instruments, platform M&A, and the long term power contracts underpinning data centre capacity
meta.method: Built from primary sources: company press releases, SEC filings, earnings calls, and reporting from Bloomberg, CNBC, DCD, and the Financial Times. Every figure carries a provenance tag: disclosed, computed from disclosed, analyst imputed, or not disclosed. Ratios are computed, never taken from secondary summaries.
meta.sourcePolicy: Each record links to the primary source where a stable public URL exists, normally the company press release or filing. Where a record is drawn from subscription reporting or where no stable link exists, the source is named in the record and no link is shown rather than linking to an aggregator.
meta.sortNote: Deals are listed newest first within each section, by announcement date. Where only a month or year is public, the date is set to the first of that period and flagged as approximate.

ppaDeals.name: Google and Constellation, PJM uprates and fleet supply
ppaDeals.type: 20 year uprate PPA plus a 15 year fleet energy supply agreement, a technology alliance, and a framework for further resources
ppaDeals.instrument: Executed PPA for new uprate capacity, plus a supply agreement on existing output
ppaDeals.structure: A 20 year PPA for 890MW of uprates across 11 units at six Constellation sites in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, plus a 15 year supply agreement for 2.7GW from Constellation's existing PJM fleet. Constellation invests more than $4.3B in the uprates. A five year technology alliance deploys Google's Gemini Enterprise at Constellation, and a framework covers other clean generation, storage and demand response.
ppaDeals.capexFlag: Computed: $4.3B over 890MW of uprates, about $4,830 per kW. Constellation says 'more than $4.3B', so this is a floor.
ppaDeals.firstPower: First uprate by 2028; programme complete by 2032
ppaDeals.note: Do not add the 2.7GW supply agreement to new capacity: it is existing fleet output. The 890MW of uprates is the new capacity. Bundles a commercial technology sale (Gemini Enterprise) with the power contract, the first record in the book where the offtaker sells its own product back to the generator.

provenance.disclosed: 890MW uprates, 11 units at six sites, 20 year PPA, 2.7GW 15 year supply agreement, more than $4.3B investment, first uprate by 2028, five year technology alliance
provenance.computedFromDisclosed: about $4,830 per kW of uprate capacity
provenance.notDisclosed: price, MW by plant, regulatory approvals

Comprises 2,176MW from the operating Perry and Davis Besse plants in Ohio, plus 433MW of incremental capacity from uprates at Perry, Davis Besse, and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania. Update Oct 2026: the DOE conditional commitment of up to $4.2B supports the same 433MW of uprates and 20 years of operation beyond current licences. The DOE release does not mention Meta, so the federal loan and the Meta PPA are separate layers financing the same new capacity.

financingDeals.structure: Independent financing platforms intended to mobilise more than $500 billion of third party capital over time to fund AI factory buildout. Morgan Stanley arranged the vehicle, described in reporting as an adaptation of the Boeing and GE vendor financing model for aircraft and engines. structuralPatterns: Vendor residual value support is being standardised and priced. Broadcom's support on the Compute SPV covered roughly 86 percent of a $35 billion financing. Nvidia has since announced platforms capping its own residual value support at 25 percent of an opportunity, explicitly describing that as substantially lower than other compute financing arrangements. The instrument is the same; the coverage level is now a competitive variable.

Credit support is compensated with equity or equity linked instruments rather than cash fees: Meta at 20 percent of Hyperion, Equinix xScale at 80/20, Google penny warrants in TeraWulf, Google at roughly 20 percent of the Nexus Hubbard project.
Guarantees are written options, not accommodations. Google marks a $44B maximum exposure at $815MM carrying value, implying an expected payout probability under 2 percent.

The cost of capital spread is the price of the wrapper: Google backed data centre projects borrowed at a median 7.1 percent against 9.3 percent for neocloud operators around Nvidia chips, roughly 220 basis points.
Chips and buildings are financed separately, by different parties, on different instruments. Private credit owns the silicon and leases it; investment grade balance sheets guarantee the real estate.
Silicon runs roughly 3.5x steel per megawatt: approximately $35M per MW for TPU hardware against approximately $10M per MW for standard air cooled shell construction.
Behind the meter generation is displacing utility interconnection as the power route, moving the binding constraint from transmission to gas pipeline capacity.
Sovereign capital has entered the stack, with recoupment then residual split structures that mirror preferred return and promote waterfalls.

Headline nuclear capacity is mostly not contracted capacity. Across the announced hyperscaler nuclear deals, roughly 5.1GW sits under executed PPAs on operating or restarting plants, while the remainder of the widely cited 9.8GW consists of development funding, options, and in one case a memorandum of understanding. Instrument classification changes the number by nearly half.

Regulators are pushing co located load back onto the grid. The Amazon and Talen arrangement at Susquehanna converted from a behind the meter co located structure to a front of the meter supply arrangement with the utility responsible for transmission, which is the clearest signal available that bypassing grid cost allocation is not a settled strategy.

The wrapper spread widened rather than compressed in August 2026. Two same borrower comparisons price the investment grade offtaker at roughly 300 to 325 basis points: CoreWeave at SOFR plus 225 against SOFR plus 550, and IREN at 6.0 percent against 9.0 percent. A lab offtaker without a rating sits wider still, with Volta's Anthropic backed loan above 11 percent and a coupon step down if Anthropic becomes investment grade.

A hyperscaler guarantee does not remove completion risk. CleanSpark's Meta guaranteed Sandersville bond priced at about 8.25 percent and junk ratings, against about 7.2 percent for QTS's investment grade Project Odyssey bonds, both on hyperscaler leases. The difference is the developer.

Google's power strategy shifted in Q3 2026 to utility structures: Black Hills' private microgrid and $399M of equipment prepayments, DTE's minimum bill and termination payment, a Georgia Power tariff product and Constellation uprates. The customer pays for the build directly, and the protection sits in the tariff rather than the PPA.
Equity is now paid for power and demand as well as credit: Vistra takes 5 percent of a Texas data centre for supply, and Amazon takes warrants in Generac for buying up to $8B of generators.
openQuestions: Does the wrapper spread compress as the structure becomes standard? Through August 2026 it widened, to roughly 300 to 325 basis points in same borrower comparisons.
Do Compute SPV style tranches ever trade or get rated, creating a public price for TPU and GPU residual risk?
Does gas pipeline capacity become the next queue, or does behind the meter simply relocate the constraint?
How much of announced capacity converts to energized capacity, against a historical 24 to 40 percent range?
Does the ratepayer protection language now appearing in these agreements, stating that local customers bear no cost for the power the buyer purchases, become a standard condition of approval?
